a-fool-and-his-money: George Barr McCutcheon, the bestselling author of Graustark romances, spins a lighthearted tale of sudden wealth and the trouble it brings. His hero must navigate schemers, flatterers, and romantic misunderstandings as money upends his ordinary life. Written in McCutcheon's breezy, good-natured style, the novel is pure early-twentieth-century escapism — funny, romantic, and quickly paced.
locusts-and-wild-honey: John Burroughs, America's best-loved nature writer of the 1800s, gathers essays on bees, birds, and country life in this warm collection. He writes about tracking wild honeybees through the woods and watching spring return to the Catskills with the eye of a born observer. The book helped create American nature writing, teaching readers to pay close attention to the wild near home.
the-story-of-the-odyssey: Scholar Alfred Church retells Homer's great epic in clear prose for young readers. Follow Odysseus through ten years of wandering after the fall of Troy — the Cyclops, the Sirens, the long voyage home to faithful Penelope. Church keeps the wonder of the original while making the ancient tale easy to follow, a perfect first meeting with one of literature's greatest heroes.
uneasy-money: Wodehouse spins comic gold from a will with impossible conditions: Bill Dawlish inherits a fortune only if he gives up his beloved football. Meanwhile a chorus of schemers circles the money. Mistaken identities and romantic tangles pile up in this breezy tale of wealth that brings nothing but trouble.
mrs-shelley: Lucy Madox Brown Rossetti — daughter of Ford Madox Brown — writes the life of Mary Shelley for the Eminent Women series. The author of Frankenstein appears as daughter, wife, widow, and working writer, navigating scandal and sorrow with courage. A sympathetic Victorian biography of a remarkable woman.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-corv: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Corvey — the imperial abbey of Saxony, famed for its library — recounts its princely history. George Cyprian Alston details its Carolingian glory. A strong reference on German monasticism. Saxon emperors prized its scriptorium above all others.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey: This 1913 reference piece treats the abbey itself — what a monastery is, how abbots rule, and how houses grew. Henry Birt covers the whole subject with learned care. Monks, nuns, and canons all find their place here. The best one-stop guide to the monastic world.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achor-valley: A 1913 entry on the Valley of Achor — the vale of trouble, where Achan was stoned. Wendell Reilly maps its somber site. Hosea promised it as a door of hope. Judgment turned to promise. Joshua's lot fell there by the Jordan. Its stones still mark the solemn place.
